Doctor Strange
2016 American superhero film based on the Marvel Comics character of the same name; produced by Marvel Studios and distributed by Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures; fourteenth film of the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU); directed by Scott Derrickson and stars Benedict Cumberbatch as Stephen Strange.

Comics publisher whose character of the same name is the basis for Doctor Strange.

Marvel Studios
Production company for Doctor Strange.

Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures
Distributor of Doctor Strange.

Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU)
Film franchise of which Doctor Strange is the fourteenth film.

Scott Derrickson
Director of Doctor Strange; wrote the film with Jon Spaihts and C. Robert Cargill.
Scott Derrickson directed Sinister and co-wrote it with C. Robert Cargill.

Jon Spaihts
Co-writer of Doctor Strange with Scott Derrickson and C. Robert Cargill.

C. Robert Cargill
Co-writer of Doctor Strange with Scott Derrickson and Jon Spaihts.
C. Robert Cargill co-wrote Sinister with Scott Derrickson.

Benedict Cumberbatch

surgeon

A Kiss for Corliss
A 1949 American comedy film directed by Richard Wallace and written by Howard Dimsdale; it stars Shirley Temple in her final starring role and final film appearance; it is a sequel to the 1945 film Kiss and Tell; it was retitled Almost a Bride before release; it was released on November 25, 1949, by United Artists.

Richard Wallace
Director of A Kiss for Corliss.

Howard Dimsdale
Writer of A Kiss for Corliss.

Shirley Temple
Stars in A Kiss for Corliss in her final starring role and final film appearance.

Kiss and Tell
1945 film to which A Kiss for Corliss is a sequel.

Almost a Bride
Title to which A Kiss for Corliss was retitled before release; this title appears in the title sequence.

United Artists
Released A Kiss for Corliss on November 25, 1949.

November 25, 1949
Release date of A Kiss for Corliss by United Artists.

Ravi
South Korean rapper, songwriter and producer signed under Jellyfish Entertainment. He began his career as a rapper in 2012 in VIXX and later formed VIXX LR with band mate Leo in 2015. His songwriting career began with co-writing VIXX's debut single "Super Hero"; as of November 2016, with the release of "VIXX 2016 Conception Ker", he had contributed to the writing and composing of over 46 songs recorded by VIXX, and he is known for composing and songwriting rap portions for the group as well as lyrics and music.

Jellyfish Entertainment
Company under which Ravi is signed.

VIXX
South Korean boy group in which Ravi began his career as a rapper in 2012. Ravi co-wrote its debut single "Super Hero" and, as of November 2016, had contributed to the writing and composing of over 46 songs recorded by VIXX; he is known for composing and songwriting rap portions for the group.

VIXX LR
VIXX's first sub-unit, formed by Ravi with band mate Leo in 2015.

Leo
Band mate of Ravi; with Ravi formed VIXX LR in 2015.

Super Hero
VIXX's debut single, co-written by Ravi.

VIXX 2016 Conception Ker
Release from November 2016 cited in connection with Ravi's contribution to over 46 songs recorded by VIXX.

rapper
Occupation of Ravi; he began his career as a rapper in 2012 in VIXX.

songwriter
Occupation of Ravi; his songwriting career began with co-writing VIXX's debut single "Super Hero".

producer
Occupation of Ravi; he is described as a producer signed under Jellyfish Entertainment.

2007 MasterCard Memorial Cup
The 2007 MasterCard Memorial Cup was played in May 2007 in Vancouver, British Columbia, at the Pacific Coliseum; it was the 89th annual Memorial Cup competition.

Memorial Cup
Annual competition referred to in the document; the 2007 edition was the 89th annual Memorial Cup competition and determined the major junior ice hockey champion of the Canadian Hockey League.

Canadian Hockey League
The CHL, whose major junior ice hockey champion was determined by the 2007 Memorial Cup tournament.

Vancouver
City in British Columbia where the 2007 MasterCard Memorial Cup was played in May 2007.

British Columbia
Province mentioned with Vancouver as the location of the 2007 MasterCard Memorial Cup.

Pacific Coliseum
Venue in Vancouver, British Columbia, where the 2007 MasterCard Memorial Cup was played.

May 2007
Month and year in which the 2007 MasterCard Memorial Cup was played.

Medicine Hat Tigers
WHL champion and participant in the 2007 Memorial Cup; defeated 3–1 by the Vancouver Giants in the second all-WHL final in tournament history.

Plymouth Whalers
OHL champion and participant in the 2007 Memorial Cup.

Lewiston Maineiacs
QMJHL champion and participant in the 2007 Memorial Cup.

Vancouver Giants
Host team and tournament champion of the 2007 Memorial Cup; won their first Memorial Cup by defeating Medicine Hat 3–1 and were competing in their second consecutive national junior championship.

WHL
League whose champion, Medicine Hat Tigers, competed in the 2007 Memorial Cup; the final was the second all-WHL final.

OHL
League whose champion, Plymouth Whalers, competed in the 2007 Memorial Cup.

QMJHL
League whose champion, Lewiston Maineiacs, competed in the 2007 Memorial Cup.

Memorial Cup attendance record
Record set by the 2007 tournament with 121,561 fans attending the nine games; the previous record was 84,686, set at the 2003 tournament in Quebec City.

2003 tournament
Tournament in Quebec City at which the previous Memorial Cup attendance record of 84,686 was set.

Quebec City
City where the 2003 tournament set the previous Memorial Cup attendance record of 84,686.

For Against
A United States post-punk/dream pop band from Lincoln, Nebraska; despite lineup shuffles and periods of dormancy, it has produced material steadily from its 1984 inception to the present.

United States
Country associated with For Against, described as a United States band.
Country where the film was released on DVD on April 17, 2007.
Country in which Mendocino County was the first jurisdiction to ban cultivation, production or distribution of GMOs.

Lincoln, Nebraska
Location from which For Against comes.

1984
Year of For Against's inception.

Index Magazine
Prominent New York City-based publication with in-depth interviews with prominent figures in art and culture; created by Peter Halley and Bob Nickas in 1996, running until late 2005; covered the burgeoning Indie culture of the 1990s and featured interviews with rising and established figures.

New York City

City where LaChapelle's Artists and Prostitutes 1985–2005 exhibit was held and where Lepore participated in a voyeuristic life-sized set.

Eenasul Fateh
Eenasul Fateh was born on 3 April 1959; also known by his stage name Aladin; described as a Bangladeshi-British cultural practitioner, magician, live artist and former international management consultant.

Amanda Lepore
Amanda Lepore (born November 21, 1967) is an American transgender model, celebutante, singer, and performance artist; a former Club Kid; a regular subject and muse in David LaChapelle's work; a participant in LaChapelle's Artists and Prostitutes 1985–2005 exhibit in New York City; and a recording artist who released singles and a debut album.

Club Kid
Lepore is described as a former Club Kid.

David LaChapelle
Photographer whose work regularly features Amanda Lepore as a subject and muse; creator of the Artists and Prostitutes 1985–2005 exhibit.

Artists and Prostitutes 1985–2005
David LaChapelle exhibition in New York City; Amanda Lepore participated and "lived" in a voyeuristic life-sized set.

Cazwell
Artist with whom Amanda Lepore wrote and/or recorded many of her singles.

I...Amanda Lepore
Amanda Lepore's debut studio album, released in 2011 on Peace Bisquit.

Peace Bisquit
Label on which Amanda Lepore's debut studio album I...Amanda Lepore was released.

November 21, 1967
Date of Amanda Lepore's birth.

Just Another Romantic Wrestling Comedy
A 2006 film starring April Hunter and Joanie Laurer; premiered in New Jersey and New York City on December 1, 2006; released on DVD in the United States and United Kingdom on April 17, 2007; won an Honorable Mention at the New Jersey International Festival awards; its release is handled by Victory Multimedia.

April Hunter
Actor starring in Just Another Romantic Wrestling Comedy.

Joanie Laurer
Actor starring in Just Another Romantic Wrestling Comedy.

New Jersey
Location where the film premiered on December 1, 2006.

United Kingdom
Country where the film was released on DVD on April 17, 2007.

DVD
Format for the film's release in the United States and United Kingdom on April 17, 2007; the DVD release is mentioned in connection with the film's award.

Victory Multimedia
Company handling the release.

New Jersey International Festival awards
Awards event at which the film won an Honorable Mention.

Honorable Mention
Award won by the film at the New Jersey International Festival awards.

Romantic comedy film
Genre description applied to the film.

Sinister
Sinister is a 2012 supernatural horror film directed by Scott Derrickson and written by Derrickson and C. Robert Cargill.

Ethan Hawke
Ethan Hawke stars in Sinister as fictional true-crime writer Ellison Oswalt.

Ellison Oswalt
Ellison Oswalt is a fictional true-crime writer who discovers a box of home movies in his attic that puts his family in danger.

box of home movies
A box of home movies discovered by Ellison Oswalt in his attic; the discovery puts his family in danger.

Cho Kyu-hyun
Born February 3, 1988; better known mononymously as Kyuhyun; South Korean singer and musical theatre actor; member of Super Junior, Super Junior-K.R.Y. and Super Junior-M; former member of S.M. the Ballad; one of the first four Korean artists to appear on Chinese postage stamps.

Kyuhyun
Mononymous name by which Cho Kyu-hyun is better known.

Super Junior
South Korean boy group of which Cho Kyu-hyun is a member.

Super Junior-K.R.Y.
Sub-group of Super Junior of which Cho Kyu-hyun is a member.

Super Junior-M

S.M. the Ballad
South Korean ballad group of which Cho Kyu-hyun is a former member.

Chinese postage stamps

singer

The Hork-Bajir Chronicles
The second companion book to the Animorphs series, written by K. A. Applegate; it is introduced by Tobias and takes place before The Pretender in series continuity, with its events occurring between The Ellimist Chronicles and The Andalite Chronicles.

Animorphs
The book series to which The Hork-Bajir Chronicles is the second companion book.
Animorphs is a science fantasy series of young adult books written by Katherine Applegate and Michael Grant under the name K. A. Applegate and published by Scholastic.

K. A. Applegate
Author of The Hork-Bajir Chronicles.
K. A. Applegate is the name under which Katherine Applegate and Michael Grant write together.

The Pretender
Book #23 in the Animorphs series; The Hork-Bajir Chronicles takes place before it with respect to continuity within the series.

The Ellimist Chronicles
One boundary named for when the events told in The Hork-Bajir Chronicles occur.

The Andalite Chronicles
One boundary named for when the events told in The Hork-Bajir Chronicles occur.

Tobias
Introduces The Hork-Bajir Chronicles and flies to the valley of the free Hork-Bajir, where Jara Hamee tells him a story.

valley of the free Hork-Bajir
Place to which Tobias flies; Jara Hamee tells him the story there.

free Hork-Bajir
Hork-Bajir group associated with the valley to which Tobias flies.

Jara Hamee
Tells Tobias the story of how the Yeerks enslaved the Hork-Bajir and how Aldrea and Dak Hamee tried to save their world; his story is narrated from the points of view of Aldrea, Dak Hamee, and Esplin 9466.

Yeerks
The group that enslaved the Hork-Bajir.

Hork-Bajir
People/race enslaved by the Yeerks; Dak Hamee is a Hork-Bajir, and Aldrea and Dak Hamee tried to save their world from the invasion.

Aldrea
An Andalite and companion of Dak Hamee who tried to save their world from the invasion; one point-of-view narrator of Jara Hamee's story.

Andalite
Species to which Aldrea belongs.

Dak Hamee
A Hork-Bajir and companion of Aldrea who tried to save their world from the invasion; one point-of-view narrator of Jara Hamee's story.

Esplin 9466
One point-of-view narrator of Jara Hamee's story.

Megamorphs
Books whose alternating narration style is compared to Jara Hamee's story.

Jara Hamee's story
Story told by Jara Hamee, narrated from the points of view of Aldrea, Dak Hamee, and Esplin 9466 and alternating in similar fashion to the Megamorphs books.

Management consulting
The practice of helping organizations improve their performance, operating primarily through the analysis of existing organizational problems and the development of plans for improvement.

Organizations
Entities that management consulting helps to improve their performance; they may draw upon the services of management consultants for reasons including gaining external advice and access to specialized expertise.

Management consultants
Service providers whose services organizations may draw upon for a number of reasons, including gaining external advice and access to the consultants' specialized expertise.

Performance
What organizations are helped to improve through management consulting.

Organizational problems
Existing problems analyzed in management consulting.

Plans for improvement
Plans developed through management consulting.

External advice
Advice that organizations may gain through the services of management consultants; described as external and presumably objective.

Specialized expertise
Consultants' expertise to which organizations may gain access through their services.

Mendocino County
California county that was the first jurisdiction in the United States to ban the cultivation, production or distribution of GMOs; after enactment it was added to an international list of GMO free zones.

California
State where Mendocino County is located.

genetically modified organisms (GMOs)
Genetically modified organisms; Mendocino County banned their cultivation, production or distribution, and risks to human health and the ecosystem were contended not fully understood.

Measure H
Ordinance entitled Measure H, passed by referendum on March 2, 2004; it is the ordinance banning cultivation, production or distribution of GMOs.

referendum
Process by which Measure H was passed on March 2, 2004.

March 2, 2004
Date on which Measure H was passed by referendum.

GMO Free Mendocino
Group that initiated the campaign for Measure H.

campaign
Highly publicized grassroots effort initiated by GMO Free Mendocino and by local farmers and environmental groups.

local farmers
Local farmers who were part of the grassroots campaign and contended that GMO risks to human health and the ecosystem are not fully understood.

environmental groups
Environmental groups that were part of the grassroots campaign and contended that GMO risks to human health and the ecosystem are not fully understood.

biotechnology industry
Industry whose interest groups opposed the measure.

California Plant Health Association
Interest group that opposed the measure; now the Western Plant Health Association.

Western Plant Health Association
Current name of the California Plant Health Association.

CropLife America
Washington-based consortium that opposed the measure; its clients represent some of the largest food distributors in the nation, including Monsanto, DuPont and Dow Chemical.

Washington
Location of CropLife America, a consortium.

Monsanto
Named in connection with CropLife America's clients, which represent some of the largest food distributors in the nation.

DuPont
Named in connection with CropLife America's clients, which represent some of the largest food distributors in the nation.

Dow Chemical
Named in connection with CropLife America's clients, which represent some of the largest food distributors in the nation.

GMO free zones
International list of GMO free zones to which Mendocino County was added after enactment of the ordinance.

pre-emptive statutes
Statutes banning local municipalities from such ordinances; they have become widespread with adoption in sixteen states.

sixteen states
States where pre-emptive statutes banning local municipalities from such ordinances have been adopted.

local municipalities
Local municipalities banned by pre-emptive statutes from such ordinances.

Amherst
A town in Hampshire County, Massachusetts, United States, in the Connecticut River valley; as of the 2010 census its population was 37,819, making it the largest municipality in Hampshire County; home to Amherst College, Hampshire College, and the University of Massachusetts Amherst, three of the Five Colleges; its name is pronounced without the "h" as "AM-erst".

Hampshire County
County in Massachusetts, United States; Amherst is a town in it and is its largest municipality, although its county seat is Northampton.

Massachusetts
U.S. state in which Hampshire County and Amherst are located.

Connecticut River valley
Valley in which Amherst is located.

Northampton
County seat of Hampshire County, Massachusetts.

Amherst College
College in Amherst and one of the Five Colleges.

Hampshire College
College in Amherst and one of the Five Colleges.

University of Massachusetts Amherst
University in Amherst and one of the Five Colleges.

Five Colleges
Consortium of which Amherst College, Hampshire College, and the University of Massachusetts Amherst are three members.

2010 census
Census as of which Amherst's population was 37,819.

AM-erst
Pronunciation of Amherst without the "h".

only the 'h' is silent
Local saying arising from Amherst's pronunciation and its politically active populace.

politically active populace
Amherst's politically active populace, referenced by the local saying about the silent "h".

Gumbo
Gumbo is the fourth and first self-released studio album by American singer-songwriter PJ Morton; it was released on April 14, 2017 by Morton Records as the follow-up to New Orleans (2013). The record incorporates R&B styles with elements of older soul music, its lyrics discuss romance and explore political and personal themes, it is entirely produced by Morton, features guest appearances by Pell, BJ the Chicago Kid and The HamilTones, and includes a cover of the Bee Gees' 'How Deep Is Your Love'.

PJ Morton
American singer-songwriter; Gumbo is his fourth and first self-released studio album, and he entirely produced Gumbo himself.

Morton Records
Record label that released Gumbo on April 14, 2017.

New Orleans
PJ Morton's third studio album, associated with 2013 in the text; Gumbo is described as its follow-up.

April 14, 2017
Release date of Gumbo.

R&B
Music style whose styles are incorporated into Gumbo; also used to describe Anthony Hamilton as an R&B singer.

soul music

romance

Bee Gees

How Deep Is Your Love

Shirley Temple Black
Shirley Temple Black (April 23, 1928 – February 10, 2014) was an American actress, singer, dancer, businesswoman, and diplomat; she was Hollywood's number one box-office draw as a child actress from 1935 to 1938; as an adult she was named United States ambassador to Ghana and Czechoslovakia and served as Chief of Protocol of the United States.

Lord High Treasurer
A post that was an English government position and has been a British government position since the Acts of Union of 1707; also called Lord Treasurer.

Lord Treasurer
Alternative name for the post of Lord High Treasurer.

English government position
A government position that the post of Lord High Treasurer was.

British government position
A government position that the post of Lord High Treasurer has been since the Acts of Union of 1707.

Acts of Union of 1707
The Acts of Union of 1707; the post of Lord High Treasurer has been a British government position since then.

holder of the post
A holder of the post of Lord High Treasurer; would be the third-highest-ranked Great Officer of State, below the Lord High Steward and the Lord High Chancellor.
